ca_lover_s_leap.blurb: A big granite cliff beside Highway 50 near Strawberry, in the Lake Tahoe region at about 5,800 feet. The wall rises from roughly 250 to nearly 600 feet, crossed by hundreds of cracks and thousands of horizontal dikes that give rests and holds, so routes feel friendlier than the steepness suggests. Trad dominates, with up to four pitches and mostly walk-off descents, plus a few sport lines (mostly 5.10 and harder) and some boulder problems. Grades center on 5.9 to 5.11, with a strong supply of 5.7 and 5.8 moderates. Climbing is generally possible from spring through fall, and summer weekends can be busy. Main areas: Main Formation, Hogsback, Lower Buttress and Dear John Buttress.

az_3_windy_point_east.blurb: Windy Point East lies along the Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains above Tucson, at about 6,000 feet near a popular overlook of the valley. It is split into dozens of small crags, fins, pinnacles and towers, and most of the cliffs face east. Trad and sport routes are about evenly matched, with a little top-roping and bouldering. Grades center on 5.10 and 5.11, with a strong 5.12 group, a few 5.13s and a modest supply of easier climbs from 5.6 to 5.9. Crags vary in elevation and aspect, so comfortable microclimates exist in all but the hottest times of year. Larger sections include Rupley Towers, Turret Rock, Punch and Judy Towers and Wind Wall.

ok_quartz_mountain.blurb: Quartz Mountain is a granite climbing area in southwest Oklahoma, north of Altus, in the western extension of the Wichita Mountains. Trad routes are the most numerous, followed by bouldering and a solid share of sport routes. Grades span 5.6 to 5.13, concentrated around 5.9 and 5.10, with boulder problems from easy to about V10. Face climbing is the signature, and many bolted routes are bold, with long runouts that do not behave like typical sport climbs. Most walls get morning shade and then sun for much of the day, and the area is regarded as a winter destination. Main sections include Watch Me Wall, Cedar Valley, the Entrance Boulders and Sea of Screams.

wi_west_bluff_central.blurb: Pure bouldering on the hillside above the western shore of Devil's Lake, in Wisconsin's Baraboo Range. The boulders mostly lie on an east-facing slope in talus and boulder fields, some open and sunny, others shaded by trees and undergrowth. The rock is quartzite, extremely hard, with little friction. Problems run from very easy up to V11, with the bulk between V1 and V8; slabs and a few highballs are common. This central stretch is made up of many small boulders and clusters, with Super Slab Area, Cave Rock Boulders, the 500 Foot Boulder Field and the area above it as the largest groupings.

mn_interstate_sp_taylors_falls.blurb: Climbing in the gorge of the St. Croix River at Taylors Falls, about 45 miles northeast of the Twin Cities. The park's bedrock is dark basalt from ancient lava flows, carved by glacial water into vertical cliffs around 100 feet tall and a landscape of potholes. Bouldering is the largest part, followed by trad routes and some top-roping. There are no bolted sport routes, so leaders rely on removable gear. Trad grades run from easy 5.4 to 5.13, concentrated at 5.8 to 5.10, and boulder problems mostly sit in V0 to V3 with a few much harder lines. Large sections include the Interstate State Park Bouldering area, Minnesota Strip, Pot Holes Area and Tourist Rocks. It is popular with visitors.
